extractor: read directly from the Immigration Department of Malaysia's Student Pass page
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim government wording, lowercased by the normalizer. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state.
structure_note:
ONE PAGE, ONE SOURCE — AND THAT IS THE POINT. imi.gov.my serves an identical 820-line navigation menu on every page. Its Employment Pass page has three unique lines of content inside that menu; this Student Pass page has 96 unique lines out of 267. Only pages whose content is distinct from the navigation are registered, and the comparison is what proves it — no single-page check can, because boilerplate is by definition what pages share.

TWO OTHER BODIES DECIDE BEFORE IMMIGRATION DOES. EMGS (Education Malaysia Global Services) screens academics and issues the Approval to Study letter; the Ministry of Home Affairs authorises the institution to enrol international students; only then does the Immigration Department endorse a pass. An applicant who reaches Immigration first has not started early, they have started in the wrong place.

THE ORDERING IS THE REQUIREMENT. Apply from outside Malaysia; get eVAL approval; then a single-entry visa from the eVisa portal if your nationality needs one; then enter; then a post-arrival medical within 7 days; then the institution submits for endorsement. Each step gates the next, and the page states them as a sequence.

CATEGORY DECIDES ENTITLEMENTS, NOT JUST PAPERWORK. Only master's and PhD holders may bring dependants at all. Language, training/skills and accredited centre students may bring none, and may not take the part-time work permission either. The same pass carries three different sets of rights depending on where you study.

SABAH AND SARAWAK ARE SEPARATE. They administer their own immigration and the page lists state-specific documents for them inline. Recorded as its own requirement rather than folded into the general list.
freshness_note: The Department publishes no dateModified and no body dateline; freshness reads as UNKNOWN, never fresh — the rule Germany set. What the page does carry is a live server clock in its own header (it rendered 'saturday : august 22, 2026' when fetched) and current-scheme references: the STARS system, the EMGS portal, and the eVisa portal's stated exclusion of applications from Malaysia, Israel and North Korea. Corroboration, recorded as corroboration.
not_extracted: The Employment Pass, the Professional Visitor Pass and the Residence Pass, which are separate routes on separate pages. The Employment Pass page in particular is registered NOWHERE: it is 3 unique lines inside the site menu, and the Department devolves the decision to the Expatriate Committee and sector regulators without publishing their criteria.
Visa fees. The Department states only that they 'vary by country' and links a rates table; no figure is invented from that.
EMGS's own academic screening criteria and the Approval to Study process. A different body's rules on a different site.
The MOHA authorisation process for institutions. It binds the school, not the student, and the student can only check whether their institution already holds it.
Renewal, cancellation and the Special Pass. This route covers a first Student Pass.
The dependants' and guardians' own Social Visit Pass conditions beyond who is eligible and the RM90 fee — those sit on the Long-Term Social Visit Pass page.

requirements.label: You must be outside Malaysia when the application is submitted
requirements.description: Not a preference. A student already in the country on another pass cannot start this route from inside it.
requirements.source_excerpt: d. applicants must be outside malaysia at the time of application submission.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: d. Applicants MUST BE OUTSIDE MALAYSIA at the time of application submission.

requirements.label: Your institution must already be approved to enrol international students
requirements.description: Public universities qualify directly. A private higher education institution needs its courses and establishment approved by MOHE and separate MOHA authorisation to enrol international students; a language, training/skills or accredited centre needs MOE and MOHR registration plus the same MOHA authorisation. This is the school's status, checkable before you apply and not fixable by you.
requirements.source_excerpt: b. admission to private higher education institutions (ipts) with courses and establishment approved by the ministry of higher education (mohe), and authorized to enrol international students by the ministry of home affairs (moha).
requirements.source_excerpt_display: b. Admission to Private Higher Education Institutions (IPTS) with courses and establishment approved by the Ministry of Higher Education (MOHE), and authorized to enrol international students by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MOHA).

requirements.label: EMGS screens you academically and issues the Approval to Study letter first
requirements.description: Applications go through the STARS system or the EMGS portal. Only eligible applicants get the letter, and without it nothing reaches Immigration.
requirements.source_excerpt: applications may be submitted online by institutions or students via the stars system or emgs portal ... emgs will conduct academic screening and issue the approval to study for international student letter only to eligible applicants.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Applications may be submitted online by institutions or students via the STARS system or EMGS portal ... EMGS will conduct academic screening and issue the Approval to Study for International Student letter only to eligible applicants.

requirements.label: After eVAL approval, apply for a single-entry visa on the official eVisa portal if your nationality needs one
requirements.description: The Department names the portal exclusively. Travel document and security checks happen at the eVAL stage, after EMGS forwards the file.
requirements.source_excerpt: f. upon obtaining eval approval, applicants from countries requiring a visa
requirements.source_excerpt_display: f. Upon obtaining eVAL approval, applicants from countries requiring a visa

requirements.label: eVisa applications cannot be made from Malaysia, Israel or North Korea
requirements.description: Worldwide otherwise. Being physically in one of the three at application time blocks the route, which compounds with the rule that you must apply from outside Malaysia.
requirements.source_excerpt: g. note: evisa applications can be made worldwide, except from malaysia, israel, and north korea
requirements.source_excerpt_display: g. Note: eVISA applications can be made worldwide, except from Malaysia, Israel, and North Korea

requirements.label: A post-arrival medical examination within 7 days of arriving
requirements.description: Seven days from landing, not from enrolment. The pass is not endorsed until it is passed and EMGS issues its support letter.
requirements.source_excerpt: h. upon arrival in malaysia, students must undergo a post-arrival medical examination within 7 days.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: h. Upon arrival in Malaysia, students must undergo a Post-Arrival Medical Examination within 7 days.

requirements.label: Your institution submits for endorsement at the immigration office nearest to it
requirements.description: The last step is the school's, not yours, and it is tied to the school's address rather than your own.
requirements.source_excerpt: i. after passing the medical examination and receiving emgs support letter, institutions may submit applications to the immigration office nearest to the institution’s address for student pass endorsement and issuance.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: i. After passing the medical examination and receiving EMGS support letter, institutions may submit applications to the Immigration Office nearest to the institution’s address for Student Pass endorsement and issuance.

requirements.label: Only master's and PhD students may bring dependants
requirements.description: Undergraduates may not, whatever their circumstances. Eligible dependants are a spouse, biological, step or adopted children under 18, disabled children of any age certified by a specialist, biological parents and parents-in-law.
requirements.source_excerpt: g. only student pass holders at master’s or phd level are permitted to bring dependents to reside in malaysia.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: g. Only Student Pass holders at Master’s or PhD level are permitted to bring dependents to reside in Malaysia.

requirements.label: Language, training/skills and accredited centre students may bring no dependants at all
requirements.description: A second, independent bar on top of the degree-level rule.
requirements.source_excerpt: i. student pass holders under the language centre, training/skills centre, and accredited centre category are not permitted to bring dependents.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: i. Student Pass holders under the Language Centre, Training/Skills Centre, and Accredited Centre category are not permitted to bring dependents.

requirements.label: Dependants and guardians may not work, do business, or take part in political activity
requirements.description: The Department lists the same restriction twice, once for dependants and once for guardians, and it includes political speeches and lectures.
requirements.source_excerpt: h. dependents are not allowed to work, conduct business, deliver political speeches, lectures, or engage in political activities.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: h. Dependents are NOT ALLOWED to work, conduct business, deliver political speeches, lectures, or engage in political activities.

requirements.label: Part-time work is capped at 20 hours a week, and only at named kinds of workplace
requirements.description: Restaurants, petrol stations, mini markets, hotels and university or college areas. Only university and private higher education students qualify; centre students do not.
requirements.source_excerpt: b. student pass holders are allowed to work part-time during their study period, limited to 20 hours per week, only at approved locations:
requirements.source_excerpt_display: b. Student Pass holders are allowed to work part-time during their study period, limited to 20 hours per week, only at approved locations:

requirements.label: Front desk duties and student recruitment work are prohibited outright
requirements.description: Two specific bans inside the part-time permission, not general conditions.
requirements.source_excerpt: c. students are prohibited from front desk duties in line with current foreign worker policies and from working as student recruitment agents.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: c. Students are prohibited from front desk duties in line with current foreign worker policies and from working as student recruitment agents.
